key_insight: A physics-informed neural network with exact boundary and initial constraints identifies the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 accurately from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable nondestructive characterization of shear electromechanical coupling for PMUT and surface acoustic wave device design.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and a resting initial state exactly.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse observations without boundary or initial-condition penalty weights.
Nondimensionalize the equations to balance coefficients and improve optimization.
evidence_signal: Constrained variants achieved 0.15–0.51% mean e15 error on manufactured data at 30 dB; the full formulation achieved 1.19% on finite-element data at 30 dB and 0.65–2.71% across 40–0 dB.
watch_item: Validation uses simulated plane-strain PZT-5H data; robustness to experimental measurements, uncertain boundary conditions, and model mismatch remains unproven.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
